label: copy-phase input "1" fed back early in the copy (recall_idx 1-3, >=3 outputs left)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the token fed back as input is the digit 1 (100% of activation mass has in_tok == 1). In other words, the model has just emitted one of the first three original tokens and it was a 1 (orig(0..2) == 1). It is restricted to the early copy steps (recall_idx 1-3; almost nothing after that) and needs a longer remaining copy: to_go >= 3. Strongest activations come at recall_idx 1-2 in long sequences (L = 8-9) with many outputs left, for example 3 1 1 a m v s d p <DEL> 3 [1]. Activations get weaker as fewer outputs remain, and short sequences (L = 4-5) give weak or no activation. It never fires during the original phase, on the delimiter, on any other fed-back token (other digits or letters), or on a 1 that is fed back late in the copy. Mass is spread evenly over the output token, so it does not depend on what is being output now.

issues: The core claim checks out. All activation mass is in the copy phase with in_tok == '1' (100%, with zero activation on any other token, the delimiter, or the original phase), and in_first is always 0.

The 'recall_idx 1-3' part overclaims. recall_idx 3 holds only 5.8% of the mass. On dev, the predicate in_tok == 1 & recall_idx == 3 has precision 0.25 (4,083 of 16,059 steps fire). By L, its precision is 0.00 at L=4, 0.0004 at L=5, 0.15 at L=6, 0.35 at L=7, 0.48 at L=8 and 0.52 at L=9. Even at L=9 it fires only about half the time, and neither prev-token digit status nor in_count explains which half (precision 0.39-0.48 in every split tried). The feature is essentially about in_tok == orig(0) or orig(1) being '1', so the explanation's 'one of the first three original tokens was a 1' is wrong about the third token.

The false positives are systematic, not scattered. The test-split misses output for the original predicate is dominated by a '1' at recall_idx 3 (orig(2) == 1) that stays inactive, for example 'c d 1 f f n j i q <DEL> c d *1*' and 'q r 1 j i f e <DEL> q r *1*'. There are also short-L cases where recall_idx 1-2 is inactive: at L=4, recall_idx 1 has precision 0.39 and recall_idx 2 has precision 0.05.

The missed activations are mostly short sequences with to_go == 2, such as L=5 at recall_idx 2 (for example 'v 1 t t <DEL> v [1]'). There, to_go >= 3 cuts off real, if weak, activations. Lowering the threshold to to_go >= 2 while keeping recall_idx <= 3 gives recall 0.994 but precision 0.73, because the recall_idx 3 false positives remain.

The original predicate on test scores precision 0.812, recall 0.890, F1 0.849 and mass recall 0.952, which reproduces the reported figures. The structured predicate below raises test F1 to 0.872 and mass recall to 0.971.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input '1' fed back as one of the first two recalled tokens (orig(0) or orig(1) == 1) in sequences of length 5 or more; weaker and only sometimes at recall_idx 3 in long sequences (L >= 7)

final_label: copy-phase input '1' fed back as one of the first two recalled tokens (orig(0) or orig(1) == 1) in sequences of length 5 or more; weaker and only sometimes at recall_idx 3 in long sequences (L >= 7)
